items.content:
Last Thursday, LinkedIn removed my account. 

110k+ followers, 500+ posts. All gone.

I kept it quiet, and simply raised a ticket. 

But then the messages started flooding in: "Are you okay?" "What happened to your profile?"

I honestly didn't think anyone would care. 

Almost gave up trying to get it back.

But so many people messaged showing their support.

Yesterday, Charlie posted asking people to help. It reached:

- 40,000 impressions in just 6 hours! 
- 100s of people raised a ticket on my behalf.
- #Bringbackfatima was everywhere in the comments.

The support was unreal & it helped get my account back.

A huge thank you to LinkedIn's creator team too.

This experience reminded me why I started Link Creators Club.

Creators need to be brought together! 

There’s an army of us working in isolation. 

We’re so much more powerful together vs on our own.

- Meet your LinkedIn connections IRL.
- Take chats in the DMs from comments.
- Build connections “outside of LinkedIn” too. 

That is where the real power is. 

I cannot wait to bring together all the UK creators on 11th September again.

Thank you to everyone who showed support.

I see you. I appreciate you. 🩵

---

Did you know my account was missing before his post?

"Why are you building your brand?"

- To find clients?
- To build a reputation?
- To find business opportunities?

Your "why" determines your content strategy.

"What do you want to be known for?"

Describe how exactly you'd like to get recognized here.

- The AI guru? 
- Marketing genius?
- Leadership coach?

3. People

"Who do you want to be known to?"

Describe who exactly would you like to get discovered by.

- Your ideal client prospect, and
- Your ideal follower prospect.

If you don't have the 3Ps sorted:

- Your brand will feel weak.
- Your content will lack direction.
- Your audience won't know what you stand for.

The 3Ps don't just build a strong foundation.

They build clarity in your mind that translates into your content.

items.content:
Good "hooks" matter.

The first line of your post = 80% success.

Charlie Hills has summaized the difference between a "good" & "bad" hook brilliantly here.

👉 Good hooks have:

1. Specificity:
☒ "Here's how to grow on LinkedIn" 
☑︎ "LinkedIn changed. Your strategy should too."

2 - Engagement:
☒ "AI is changing everything"
☑︎ "ChatGPT changed. Most people didn't notice."

3 - Value Proposition
☒ "Let me share some tips"
☑︎ "I rebuilt my LinkedIn strategy from scratch. (How I went from zero to 115k+ in 494 days)"

4 - Action-Oriented Language
☒ "You might want to try this"
☑︎ "How to make a landing page in 5 minutes. Using AI and your LinkedIn profile."

5 - Relatability
☒ "Here's what I learned"
☑︎ "My AI outputs were trash for 6 months. Then I discovered these 8 prompting styles."

👉 Bad hooks have:

1 - Vagueness: "Pretty interesting topic, right?"
 
2 - Generic Questions: "Looking to grow your following?"
 
3 - Clichéd Openings: "In today's fast-paced world..."
 
4- Tentative Language: "This might work for you..." "
 
5 - Missing Value: "I have a secret to share..."

👉 Hook formulas that work:

Pattern 1: Contrast Reality "Most people [common mistake]. But [tool/method] can help you [better result]."

Pattern 2: Platform Shift "[Platform] has completely changed. The old tactics don't work anymore."

Pattern 3: Personal Discovery "I [tested/discovered/built] [specific thing]. The results: [shocking outcome]."

Pattern 4: Direct How-To "How to [achieve result] in [timeframe]. Using [specific method/tool]."

Pattern 5: Transformation Story "I went from [starting point] to [end point]. Here's exactly how I did it."

90% of LinkedIn posts are written for the author.

The top 10% are written for the reader.

3. Answer comments with depth

→ A 3 sentence answer with a tip gets remembered.

4. Share your mistakes
→ Your failures help someone else learn.
→ Vulnerability builds connection faster than credentials.

5. Celebrate others
→ Support small accounts!

When you focus on helping, the growth follows.

items.content:
Posting my digital fashion designs online honestly changed my career 😊

What started as posting my projects online led to opportunities I never imagined from Forbes 30 Under 30 and exhibiting on Oxford Street to building a community of 400,000+ people.

But even with all of those milestones, being a content creator can still feel surprisingly isolating 🥲

That's why attending CreatorFest was such a refreshing reminder that we're all figuring it out together.

I had some great conversations with creators who openly shared their challenges, lessons and strategies for growing in this evolving space.

A few standout talks for me:

• Rosie Gee & Natalie O'Neill talked about the power of newsletters and owning your community. I already have a Substack but it made me realise I haven’t given writing the attention it deserves since I’ve been so focused on video content.

• Hala Al-Ajil, Lauren Levya, Niall MacMillan 🪫🔋Currently Recharging  & Justin Girdler talked about building creator wealth beyond brand deals by creating your own IP. It was a reminder that the creator economy is still young and building something sustainable means owning your brand, audience and IP.

• Jonathan Gustavii talked about Roblox as a platform to watch, especially as younger generations increasingly socialise in immersive spaces. This really resonated with me as I’ve always been interested in the intersection between fashion and gaming.

• Fatima Khan talked about how LinkedIn is often overlooked by creators. For creator-led businesses, it’s not just about being an influencer, it’s about building influence and connecting with the right people.

• Mia McGrath talked about her journey of building a brand, standing out amongst the noise online whilst staying authentic. A reminder that not everyone has to like your opinion online but the right people will eventually find you and stay to watch.

After hearing these talks and connecting with so many creators, I’m feeling more inspired than ever to keep sharing my digital fashion journey and designs online. Watch this space ✨

And a big thank you to everyone I met and chatted with throughout the event. Kseniia Leonova Dan Biddle Ben Kaluza Jonathan Boadu Harry Anthony Bozadjian Chian Reynolds Skye Petrie Jonny Steel Hafsa Hersi Nicole C.

"What should I post today?"

If you're asking this, you don't have content pillars.

Follow this framework to build your pillars:

1. What are content pillars:

3-5 core topics you consistently post about.

They help you:
→ Stay focused (no random posts)
→ Build authority in specific areas
→ Attract the RIGHT audience
→ Never run out of ideas

2. How to choose your pillars:

Find the intersection of:
1. What you KNOW (expertise)
2. What you LOVE (passion)
3. What they NEED (audience pain points)

3. The 4-Pillar Formula:

🎯 Expertise → Teach your craft (40%)
📖 Story → Build connection (25%)
💡 Industry → Show awareness (20%)
🎭 Personal → Be relatable (15%)

4. My Pillars:

→ LinkedIn growth
→ AI tools & tutorials
→ Content creation tips
→ Personal brand building

5. How to build yours:

Step 1: List 10 topics you could talk about forever
Step 2: Cut what your audience won’t care about
Step 3: Group into 4-5 pillars
Step 4: Commit for 90 days

1 pillar = 50+ post ideas.

Save this. Build yours.

items.content:
Anthropic has released the perfect prompt guide.

Here's the full structure:

1. Task context
↳ Vague context produces vague output.
↳ Set the scene properly before you ask for anything.

2. Tone context
↳ Tell it exactly how to communicate.
↳ Every output should be specific to a team member.

3. Background data, documents, and images
↳ Feed it everything relevant (URLs, existing content, rankings)
↳ The more context it has, the sharper the output.

4. Detailed task description and rules
↳ Be specific about what you want it to focus on and what the rules are.
↳ Tell it exactly what matters and what to ignore.

5. Examples
↳ Paste in an example of the output format you want.
↳ Claude follows examples better than instructions alone.

6. Conversation history
↳ If there's previous work or feedback from earlier sessions, include it.
↳ Claude has no memory between conversations unless you give it one.

7. Immediate task description
↳ After all the context, tell it exactly what you need today.
↳ Specific, scoped, with one clear request.

8. Think step by step
↳ Ask it to reason before it responds. 
↳ This step alone dramatically improves output quality.

9. Output formatting
↳ Tell it how to structure the response before it writes anything.
↳ Summary, top priority fixes, secondary recommendations, and quick wins.

Keep this handy for your next Claude prompt. ✨

Thanks to Chris Donnelly for sharing it.
